item.title: SummerStage Founder Joe Killian Talks 40 Years of Music and Shares Some of the Best NYC Stories You’ve Never Heard
item.description:
[Intro music plays]
Host: Welcome to our podcast, where we dive into the world of music and entertainment. Today, we're talking about SummerStage, the iconic summer concert series in New York City. I'm joined by the founder, Joe Killian, who's here to share the story of how it all began.
[Soft music plays in the background]
Host: Joe, thanks for joining us. You've been instrumental in shaping the live music scene in NYC. Let's take a walk back in time to 1986, when SummerStage first started with a free Sun Ra Arkestra concert. What inspired you to create this series?
[Short pause]
Host: As we sit here in Central Park's Rumsey Playfield, it's hard not to notice the transformation of this space over the years. From a wasteland to a family-friendly green space, SummerStage has been a part of it all. Joe, you've seen it all - the perfect days, the nightmare days, and the great concert stories that come with them.
[Music transitions to a montage of SummerStage performances]
Host: Over the years, SummerStage has hosted an incredible range of artists, from James Brown and Stevie Wonder to Patti Smith and The Killers. This year's lineup is just as impressive, with Angélique Kidjo, Laurie Anderson, and De La Soul, to name a few.
[Music transitions back to the host]
Host: As we celebrate SummerStage's 40th anniversary, we look back on its humble beginnings and the vision that Joe had for a free music series that would connect all of New York City. Joe, what's next for SummerStage, and how do you see it evolving in the future?
[Outro music plays]
Host: Thanks for tuning in to our conversation with Joe Killian, the founder of SummerStage. If you're in NYC this summer, be sure to check out one of the many free concerts happening across the five boroughs. Until next time, stay tuned for more updates from the world of music and entertainment.
